name: Tryout
why: Neat few-word twist on the shop, but using a member's ability without owning it is Green's Sample job, and its value swings with whatever the shop shows.

name: Gather
why: Clear plain anchor with a recruit kicker; nobody else notices, and it is the same text as Stash and Allowance.

name: Walk-In
why: A free member in round I is a big moment, and the +1 red to each rival is a small gift the table sees.

name: Promote
why: The signature red swap: you trade up out of a rival's cult; strong aim choice, the victim still gets a member back.

name: Demote
why: Mirror of Promote that trades down; the downgrade is rarely what you want, so it mostly lives as a weaker sibling or a Foster Parents trigger.

name: Initiation
why: Round III burst anyone can grab: a free member up to 8, plain and powerful.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Every round you pick a rival member of the same cost to trade for; clear, aimed, feeds Foster Parents and Deprogrammers, and Loyalists answer it.

name: Volunteer
why: Pure filler: a cheap body for recruit triggers and the red count, but nothing happens when it lands.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two recruits for one buy, chains into Proselytizers and Recruiter; nine resources for a 3 is steep.

name: Proselytizers
why: A clean engine that pays every recruit, including red's free ones; nobody else at the table feels it.

name: Mob
why: Up to +6 a round for the red leader; rivals can race the red count, but it pays the player already ahead.

name: Recruiter
why: +1 red per recruit for six resources is a slow trickle that rarely pays back.

name: Patriarch
why: A generic member-count scorer, the same shape as Timekeeper and Snobs, rewarding the big cult.

name: Foster Parents
why: Rides on every swap red already does (Promote, Demote, Body Snatchers, Poach) and makes rivals think twice before trading with you.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Good link to the swap cards, but a cost of 3 for 4 followers and 4 red members is an always-buy.

name: Panel
why: A swap on recruit that combos with Foster Parents and Deprogrammers; "promote or demote" asks a new player to know two spaces.

name: Loyalists
why: A clear block against red's swaps and Body Snatchers; rivals see it and aim elsewhere.

name: Clerk
why: +1 red each round for five resources: forgettable, never the right pick.

name: Sleep In
why: A big purple pile, paid for by placing last; the token and its timing take a rules read.

name: Hold Up
why: The skip lands on whoever is next, even you, so timing is a real call and the victim can see it coming.

name: Right Away
why: Two turns in a row in one breath; feeds Courier and Hot Streak, small gain on its own.

name: Last Call
why: A big payoff for holding minions back, at the cost of going last; the token rules make it a read.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row: a big change to the snake in few words, and it sets up Courier and Hot Streak.

name: Overtime
why: A round III extra minion: plain, and a burst any player can use.

name: Courier
why: A full spread of colors on each double turn, feeding yellow sets; "consecutive turn" needs a ruling on snake ends.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays when a rival takes the Goes Last token; rarely fires and is hard to aim.

name: Bell Ringer
hardFail: Unclear and untrackable: needs the table to remember when the token was placed relative to a skip
why: Nobody could say when this fires, and the table can't track "placed before the skip".

name: Night Owls
why: An extra minion every round from round II is a real rule bend; eight resources is a lot.

name: Early Birds
why: A cheap answer to Hold Up and Bouncers that a first-timer gets at once.

name: Bouncers
why: Skipping the next two rivals on recruit is a table moment with timing to choose, and feeds Gossip.

name: Gossip
why: Pays on every skipped turn, anyone's, so Hold Up and Bouncers build into it.

name: Timekeeper
why: The same per-own-color game-end scorer as Snobs and Old Money; nothing purple about it.

name: Closer
why: Pays for going last, which purple already chases; a race for the last minion the table can see.

name: Hot Streak
why: A once-a-game cash-in after a chain of turns; big when set up with Crunch Time, but counting turns in a row takes care.

name: Shift Crew
why: Four followers for four resources and nothing else: dead weight in a color about timing.

name: Toast
why: A big silver gain with a visible gift to everyone; a clean anchor for the giving color.

name: Polish
why: A plain color exchange, which is Yellow's job, and nobody else notices it.

name: Party Gifts
why: Six followers for gifting three silver, with a real call about who you feed in the silver contest; strong for round I.

name: Potluck
why: Every rival pays one resource and gets two silver: a fair trade but small, and each rival has to choose on your turn.

name: Sweet Nothings
why: You give your own silver to get two of any color back each: a real hold-versus-give call on the silver contest.

name: Largesse
why: The round III gift burst; who gets the silver can swing the last silver contest, so it is a real aim.

name: Godparent
why: Give a member away for its cost in followers; pairs with Old Maid, Martyrs and Foster Parents across colors.

name: Hostesses
why: A steady giving engine every round; every gift feeds Caterer and rivals' silver.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver on gifts is too small to notice, and "gifted" (per gift or per silver) needs a ruling.

name: Toastmaster
why: A cheap way-in that pays +1 per Silver space; filler, forgettable.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling your silver once is a big, timed moment that swings the silver contest.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: A real rule bend, but it is the old gold hoard idea, and eleven resources is a lot.

name: Philanthropist
why: A one-off copy of Largesse and Party Gifts on a member; nothing new for the color.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Every Silver space can turn a cheap member into +4 followers, linking to Godparent, Old Maid and Foster Parents; strong for a cost of 3.

name: Creditor
why: Take two followers from the rival you pick and leave them three silver: a fair aimed trade you can point at the leader.

name: Debt Collectors
why: A once-a-game claw-back of the silver your own gifts handed out.

name: High Society
why: Pays when rivals take Silver spaces, so the table thinks twice; small.

name: Envy
hardFail: Relies on a rival holding more silver than you
why: Pays only when a rival out-holds you, the exact shape that is barred.

name: Harvest
why: The plain fuel anchor, in any colors, which fits a color about going broad.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads the board for a payout, but counting minions per color is a small sum for a fiddly read.

name: New Blood
why: Pays for widening into a new color; clean, but solo.

name: Housewarming
why: A free member in a new color: the yellow idea in one line.

name: Melting Pot
why: Pays for how broad you already are, which rewards the wide cult more than the one behind.

name: Makeover
why: Rearranging everything in round III swings several contests at once: a late burst anyone can use.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills in the colors you lack, so it helps a thin pile most and feeds full sets.

name: Customs Officer
why: A small defensive trickle against Magenta; doesn't move yellow's idea of going broad.

name: Tourist
why: Followers for holding a spread of colors, every round; a steady scorer that pushes you wide.

name: Harmonist
why: A game-end full-set scorer: clear, but solo and quiet.

name: Dyer
why: Tourist's text paying yellow instead of followers: a weaker sibling.

name: Meddler
why: Changing one of each rival's resources can cost them a contest; aim is real, the wording is loose.

name: Drifters
why: A cheap wild body that plugs into any color's member count; a strong way-in.

name: Big Tent
why: Pays for exactly one member per color, a sharp pull against stacking a color.

name: Caravan
why: A bigger Dyer that pays the already-broad pile more each round; rich-get-richer.

name: Jack-of-All-Trades
why: Makes full sets easier, which matters only for yellow's contest; quiet.

name: Savings
why: A scaling gain plus a chance to bury the member a rival wanted.

name: Out of Style
why: Clears a whole color out of the shop: denial the table sees, and it feeds Patroness.

name: Peek
why: A good scaling gain and your pick of the pile; private, so nobody else reacts.

name: Recruit Twice
why: An extra buy in round II: plain and strong.

name: Bury
why: A smaller Savings; the half-cost blue payout is a sum to work out.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits in round III is the burst a trailing player can grab.

name: Hawker
why: Every rival gets a priced shot at a member before you take it free; a table moment, but many words and rivals choose on your turn.

name: Patroness
why: Pays on every bury, which blue does constantly; "per member or per event" needs a ruling.

name: Snobs
why: The same own-color game-end scorer as Timekeeper and Old Money.

name: Window Shopper
why: Buries two members each round for their colors; clean denial, but who picks the two must be read.

name: Shopaholics
why: Two buys every turn is a huge rule bend; strong enough to be the first buy whenever it shows.

name: Window Dressers
why: Cheap 3-member body with a shop wipe on recruit; a second Out of Style.

name: Doormen
why: Forcing a swap on a rival every round is Red's job, and the cost rule is long.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue on follower buys has nothing to do with the shop.

name: Trendsetters
why: Each recruit churns one shop card, feeding Patroness; a cheap 3-member body.

name: Critic
why: +1 when a rival buys blue: rare and small.

name: Scavenger
hardFail: Owner chooses and pays during a rival's turn (turn-flow rule)
why: Grabbing what rivals bury is a fun counter, but you choose and pay on their turn.

name: Help Yourself
why: The core steal, scaling by round, aimed where it hurts the leader.

name: Stash
why: The same text as Gather and Allowance; nothing magenta about it.

name: Lie Low
why: A steal and a shield for the round; needs a marker on the table.

name: Heist
why: Three followers off the leader: plain, felt, a catch-up tool.

name: Shake Down
why: The victim chooses their own punishment, which feels bad, and the wording is long.

name: Poach
why: The round III member grab; clear, felt, and Martyrs and Loyalists-style answers exist.

name: Cutpurse
why: A cheap steady tax on the richest pile; no decision, but it pushes back on hoards.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap one-off steal of three; fine, flat.

name: Grifter
why: Eight resources for a one-off steal sized by your own cult size; overpriced and rewards the big cult.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A steal right before contests are scored can flip one; a timed, aimed sting you can see coming.

name: Desperado
why: Bigger steals while you trail: built-in catch-up.

name: Extortionist
why: Cutpurse doubled for more: a repeat of its sibling.

name: Bodyguards
why: A full shield that switches off theft against you, which favors the big pile.

name: Double Agent
why: A trade on recruit that feeds Foster Parents, though it is more Red's move than Magenta's.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes a member from the same rival every round from round I; the victim loses a member early with no answer.

name: Shoplifter
why: A steal on every recruit, follower buys included; a clear engine.

name: Fence
why: Pays only when a rival steals from you, which rarely happens to the magenta player.

name: Allowance
why: The same text as Gather and Stash; nothing white about it.

name: Splurge
why: Big followers on a pricey recruit, but the per-2 then per-1 math is a sum to work out.

name: Exchange
why: Turns a few resources into followers at double rate; clean, solo.

name: Farewell
why: Cash a member out for its cost in followers; pairs with Martyrs and Recluse, though it fights the fewest-followers contest.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell paying white instead of followers: a weaker sibling.

name: Cash In
why: The round III cash-out the white pile builds toward.

name: Recluse
why: Pays for staying small against rivals' cults, a clean catch-up scorer that fits white's casting-out.

name: Landlord
why: Steady white income: fine filler, nobody notices.

name: Heiresses
why: Pays per member in a color that sheds members; small and off its theme.

name: Brokers
why: +1 on every white follower payout, so white's spaces build into it.

name: Misers
why: Pays for holding white at the end against cashing it in: a real hold-or-spend call.

name: Raiders
why: A follower steal is Magenta's Heist on a white card.

name: Cashier
why: Cash In on a member; good timing call, but repeats the space.

name: Money Changers
why: Pays on every follower buy at the table; steady and quiet.

name: Martyrs
why: Leaving pays you its cost, so a rival's Poach or swap backfires and your own Farewell pays twice; plays off many colors.

name: Old Money
why: The same own-color game-end scorer as Snobs and Timekeeper.

name: Hoarder
why: Turn everything white once, setting up Cash In or Misers; a big timed moment.

name: Build Up
why: The plain fuel anchor.

name: Echo
why: Copy the previous action: scales with the board, few words.

name: Reprise
why: Copy your own best action again: clean and grows through the game.

name: Sample
why: Borrow a rival's member's On Recruit; reads the rivals' cults.

name: Cover
why: Copy an empty action, so the unused spaces still pay.

name: Greatest Hits
why: The round III payoff for a cult of On Recruit members.

name: Busker
why: Steady green income: filler.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrows a rival's ability each round; strong and aimed, but needs a marker and a read.

name: Impressionist
why: +1 on every copy at the table: too small to feel.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubles every copy you make, a strong engine with Echo and Reprise; ten resources is a lot.

name: Fan Club
why: Copies what the leader took: a clean catch-up hook.

name: Roadie
why: Income per green member, so a cheap green cult builds it.

name: Stunt Double
why: Doing your action twice on recruit makes you time your best space with the buy.

name: Tribute Band
why: Do everything a rival did this round once: a huge moment, with fourteen resources the barrier.

name: Doppelganger
why: Becomes your best member: clear, and better with the cards around it.

name: Agents
why: An anti-copy shield, a cheap answer to rival greens more than a green engine.

name: Encore
why: Doubles one On Recruit; timing the big one is a real choice.

name: Party Crasher
why: Once a game you get into the space that was already taken; a rule bend everyone feels.

name: Alchemists
why: Pay any color for members: a strong unlock for 5, worth 3.

name: Extra Hand
why: One extra minion once for nine resources: Overtime already does that.

name: Line Cutters
why: Going first every round for 2 resources and 3 followers overrides the catch-up order; a must-buy for the leader.

name: Old Maid
why: A hot potato for Godparent, Guest of Honor and Double Agent; the table laughs when it moves.

name: Dabblers
why: Wild member counts for any color's member contest; "wild" needs a ruling for the first read.

name: Anarchist
why: A swap anywhere every round is a big lever; once per round on this is a power flag.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancelling a contest you can't win is a clear, aimed, catch-up sting the leader can see coming.

name: Con Men
why: A bigger Accomplice in grey: Magenta's job.

name: Sore Loser
why: Punishes the contest leader if you go empty: clear catch-up.
